drills.q: GARCH(1,1) with alpha=0.08, beta=0.90, omega=0.002 (daily). Long-run daily vol?
drills.a: Unconditional variance = omega/(1-alpha-beta) = 0.002/0.02 = 0.01, so long-run daily vol = 1% (~15.9% annualized x sqrt(252)). Persistence 0.98 -> shock half-life ~34 days.

drills.q: Why is EWMA lambda=0.94 'GARCH without mean reversion'?
drills.a: EWMA is GARCH(1,1) with omega=0, alpha=1-lam=0.06, beta=lam=0.94: alpha+beta=1 exactly (IGARCH boundary), so variance never reverts to a fixed level - it just exponentially tracks recent shocks. Deliberately simple for overnight VaR; the price is no long-run anchor.

drills.q: Your backtest features use Kalman-SMOOTHED levels over history. What is wrong and how do you fix it?
drills.a: Smoothing uses future data relative to each historical point - leakage. Fix: use FILTERED states (only data <= t), refit variance parameters on expanding/rolling windows ending at t, and verify every feature at time t is computable from data available by t.

drills.q: PM asks why Prophet's 80% intervals missed 40% of last quarter's points. Explain and propose a fix.
drills.a: Prophet default intervals simulate future trend pivots from historical changepoint frequency - a heuristic ignoring parameter/seasonality/residual-autocorrelation uncertainty; under-coverage in volatile regimes is expected. Fix: conformal calibration on rolling one-step residuals (empirical quantiles) or quantile-loss model with empirical coverage monitoring.

drills.q: 10-day VaR from a GARCH with persistence 0.98: what is wrong with multiplying 1-day vol by sqrt(10)?
drills.a: sqrt(t) scaling assumes i.i.d. shocks; persistence 0.98 means elevated vol persists across all 10 days, so true 10-day tail risk exceeds the scaled figure materially. Correct: iterate the variance recursion h steps forward and aggregate scenario returns path-wise (filtered simulation).

drills.q: You have 300 series of 60 observations each for forecasting. Deep nets or classical - and why?
drills.a: Global deep models can work despite short per-series length because they pool across series (300x60 = 18k training windows); N-BEATS-style architectures were built exactly for this regime. Still ship an ETS/state-space challenger and seasonal-naive floor per series; promote only if weighted pinball beats floors consistently out-of-sample.

drills.q: Name two reasons TimesFM zero-shot output should not go straight into a bank's capital process.
drills.a: Interval calibration is not guaranteed (tails undertrained; coverage unverified per domain) and domain shift/microstructure dynamics differ from its web-traffic-heavy pretraining corpus - plus auditability/reproducibility requirements (SR 11-7) demand documented training lineage. Use as ensemble baseline with conformal calibration and human validation before anything capital-relevant.

drills.q: After a crash week your Gaussian-GARCH VaR understates risk. Give three upgrades.
drills.a: (1) Student-t or skewed-t innovations for fat tails; (2) GJR/EGARCH asymmetry so negative shocks feed vol harder; (3) iterate multi-day recursion instead of sqrt-scaling, or blend in realized-vol/HAR estimates if intraday data exists. Also check persistence jumped post-break - refit windows may need shortening.

drills.q: M5 was won by LightGBM with lag features. Does that make deep forecasters pointless?
drills.a: No - it makes them dataset-specific. M5 was tabular retail with rich covariates where GBMs excel; M4's univariate 100k-series setting favored pure neural architecture (N-BEATS). Decision rule: many related series + covariates + cold starts -> global models; tabular feature engineering dominates -> GBMs; single governed series -> ETS/ARIMA/state space.

drills.q: What's the practical risk of using a foundation model like TimesFM zero-shot on a financial return series, and how would you test it before trusting it?
drills.a: Foundation models are pretrained mostly on series with visible trend/seasonality (retail, web traffic); financial returns are closer to a low-signal, fat-tailed near-random-walk, so zero-shot uncertainty estimates may be miscalibrated. Test via walk-forward backtesting and check empirical coverage of quantile forecasts (does the 90% interval actually contain ~90% of realized values out of sample) before trusting it in production.

drills.q: Distinguish Prophet's changepoint trend from a Kalman local-level-plus-trend model -- aren't both just 'trend that can change'?
drills.a: Prophet's trend is piecewise linear with a small, regularized set of discrete changepoints -- a structural, sparse-jump story. A Kalman trend evolves continuously every period via process noise Q, a smooth random walk with no discrete changepoints. They can look similar smoothed but extrapolate differently: Prophet tends to extend the last growth rate more conservatively; a Kalman model with nontrivial Q keeps accumulating uncertainty every step into the future.
